support: At Tarsel the Hollin stands cold in the shed beside the platform, and the climb will never again be made behind her.

I laid my hand on her iron side and thought of the mornings, years ago, when I rode up behind her with her smoke drifting back past the carriage windows and the whole village hearing her whistle at Gessen.
WV13-P01.6.note: The author describes the working line plainly and reserves feeling for remembering the lost steam engine, a longing for the railway's past rather than worry, criticism, amusement or admiration (the description of the line is factual, not praising).

exclusions.A: Engineers found the diving tower unsound, and it was pulled down; a low new board stands at the deep end in its place.

support: When I stand at the deep end now, I still look up for a tower that is gone.
Three generations of Ostley children learned to dive from that tower, and the place where they learned has gone with it.
WV13-P02.5.note: The writer gives each loss a practical cause (unsound tower, split tiles) and blames no one, but dwells on what is gone, which is regret rather than disapproval, unease, admiration or amusement.
